subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Tactics and Strategy in Invasion Activities
title: Performance task build: reading a situation and choosing between options under transfer
focus: reading a situation and choosing between options
essentialQuestion: How do you win space before you win the ball?
privacySafeScenario: Analyze a described game situation, propose two tactical solutions with their tradeoffs, then apply one in play or in a solo simulation and evaluate the result.
studentTask: Learner works reading a situation and choosing between options against an opponent who adjusts in response, so the first plan stops working and a second has to be found mid-activity at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of reading a situation and choosing between options degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds reading a situation and choosing between options against an opponent who adjusts in response, so the first plan stops working and a second has to be found mid-activity, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Tactical understanding may be demonstrated through play, walk-through pace, a tabletop or diagram simulation, or written analysis; each route reaches the same standard.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of reading a situation and choosing between options yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Tactical understanding may be demonstrated through play, walk-through pace, a tabletop or diagram simulation, or written analysis; each route reaches the same standard.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where reading a situation and choosing between options shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
